newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia to give priority to joining EU.
newsitem.headline: Estonia to give priority to joining EU.

text.p: The Baltic state of Estonia, one of the many former Communist bloc states aiming for European Union (EU) membership, said on Tuesday it would give priority to making its legislation conform to EU standards.
Estonia, the smallest of the Baltic states, regained independence from the former Soviet Union five years ago.
It is desperate to reintegrate with the West, from which it was cut off for 50 years.
"The government decided today that all ministries will take EU integration as next year's key priority," Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi told a news conference.
"We will review the drafting of laws so those related to the EU will take precedence over purely domestic issues," he said.
Estonia has a good reputation as a reformer and like neighbours Latvia and Lithuania also hopes for NATO membership.
But the EU is seen as a more ac xczczhievable goal as Russia objects strongly to the Balts' inclusion into NATO.
"In the next six to eight months, crucial decisions will be taken on whether Estonia can join the first group of countries that are accepted to the EU," Vaehi said.
"For this reason, a concerted effort must be made on all levels of government," he added.
